findings.message:
A VENDOR file is present but no third-party library could be parsed from it. Declare each bundled library in its own block, separated from the next by a blank line. A block names the packaged file path and a source URL pointing at the exact file (on unpkg, jsDelivr, the npm registry, or a raw GitHub URL), so the file can be verified automatically. A bare repository link is not a source, and a path mentioned in a sentence is not a declaration. For example:

lib/purify.min.js:
  source: https://unpkg.com/dompurify@3.2.7/dist/purify.min.js
  licence: Apache-2.0

vendor/jszip.min.js:
  source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jszip@3.10.1/dist/jszip.min.js
  licence: MIT

A library may also be declared on a single line, and those need no blank line between them:

lib/purify.min.js: https://unpkg.com/dompurify@3.2.7/dist/purify.min.js
vendor/jszip.min.js: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jszip@3.10.1/dist/jszip.min.js

A library that ships as many files is better declared once, as the directory holding them, against a source naming the whole release - a pinned npm package, or a GitHub tree URL. Every file under the directory is then verified against that release, including the ones no line names:

directory: lib/pdfjs
source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pdfjs-dist@4.10.38/build/

Read more: https://webextension-api.thunderbird.net/en/mv3/guides/vendoring.html.

Each of the following source URLs cannot verify the file(s) declared against it. A file source verifies exactly one file, so pairing it with several is ambiguous; and a directory needs a source that can be fetched as an archive of the whole release, which the URL of a single file - or a CDN's directory listing page - is not. Give each file its own source URL, or declare the containing directory against a source that names the release: a pinned npm package (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<name>@<version>/, or its registry tarball), or a GitHub tree URL (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<ref>/<path>).
